title: Optimize Guardrails + Quality Gating — Kickoff Notes (working doc)
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture kickoff notes for the “Quality guardrails gating for Optimize” project.
- This is a working doc (not the PRD). Expect partial thoughts / open questions.

Meeting
- Date/time: 2024-11-18 10:00–11:00 PT
- Location: Zoom (recording link in calendar)

Attendees
- Product / Optimize: Aditya Rao (DRI), Marissa Cole
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Selene Huang, Sana Farid, Karthik Iyer
- Control Plane / Policy: Ethan Park, Jordan Lee, Benji Okafor
- SRE / Reliability: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes
- Telemetry / Analytics: Logan Wright
- Console / UX: Kenji Nakamura, Chloe Martin
- Security / Audit/RBAC: Naomi Feldman

Context / why we’re here
- Optimize can propose and apply cost-saving config changes (batching/caching/quantization/routing).
- We have at least a few cases where cost improvements were real but output quality regressed (format drift, tool call schema issues, “reasoning” degradation, subtle rubric score drops).
- Today, “apply” is mostly a trust-based workflow + post-hoc monitoring. This is not sufficient for enterprise workloads (and creates support load + customer churn risk).

Problem statement (v0)
- We need a mandatory gating layer so Optimize-driven changes cannot be applied unless they pass a defined evaluation suite with clear regression thresholds.
- Gating must be auditable, explainable, and operationally safe.

What does “quality regression” mean here?
- Not one thing. We need a taxonomy:
  - Task success / rubric scores (per workload)
  - Structured output / schema adherence
  - Tool-calling correctness (arguments, ordering, retries)
  - Safety constraints (toxicity / policy)
  - Factuality proxies (where applicable)
- We should avoid boiling the ocean: initial focus is on the metrics that correlate with the real customer-impact failures we’ve seen (quantization + formatting/tool correctness; batching/caching + ordering/format).

Goals (aligned in meeting)
- Prevent user-visible quality regressions when applying cost optimizations.
- Standardize prompt sets + eval suites + thresholds, with versioning and audit trail.
- Make outcomes actionable: pass/fail with reasons, links to eval artifacts, and rollback hooks.
- Provide a safe rollout path (observe-only → soft-block → hard-block).

Non-goals (explicitly called out)
- Replacing eval-harness (we extend it; we don’t rewrite it).
- Full bespoke eval authoring as a services engagement.
- Automatically picking the “best” model for a customer (out of scope; guardrails only gate config deltas).

Key early decisions / alignment
1) Where to enforce
- Decision leaning: enforce at control-plane apply path (API + Console), not in runtime.
- Rationale: auditability + consistent behavior across hosted/dedicated/private. Runtime may still enforce invariants (e.g., disallow unsafe profile transitions), but the gating decision should live in control plane.
- Action: capture as ADR (Ethan/Jordan).

2) Default behavior on gating infrastructure failures
- We need a deterministic, tier-aware safe-degrade policy.
- Initial proposal:
  - Hosted self-serve: block apply if gating cannot run (timeout/system error), with clear messaging + “retry later”.
  - Enterprise / dedicated: may allow “manual approval” pathway (restricted) with justification + audit logging, and potentially a second approver (TBD).
- SRE request: make this policy explicit in runbook; define alerting thresholds and operator steps.

3) Overrides
- Product stance: overrides must exist for high-priority enterprise incidents, but must be rare, rate-limited, and highly visible.
- Security stance: overrides require RBAC + immutable audit logs; include justification + (optional) approver.
- Open: do we require 2-person rule for certain changes (e.g., quantization)?

4) Statistical vs fixed thresholds
- Applied ML: prefer confidence-interval-aware thresholds and min sample sizes to reduce flakiness.
- Product: needs something understandable in UI (“failed: schema adherence -2.1pp vs max -0.5pp allowed; 95% CI ...”).
- Agreement: start with a small set of metrics with CI + min sample size; avoid overly complex stats in V1 UX.

System sketch (shared mental model)
- Optimize apply request → control plane policy check determines:
  - which eval suites to run (based on optimization type + workload tags + model family)
  - which thresholds apply (based on tenant tier + model family + workload)
- Eval runner executes eval-harness in “gating mode”, persists results + artifacts
- Policy engine evaluates results deterministically and returns:
  - pass/fail
  - reasons (metric, delta, threshold, sample size, CI)
  - references (eval run id, prompt-set revision, model version)
- Apply is allowed only on pass (or on override path).

Rough milestones (not a committed schedule)
- Phase 0 (Discovery, ~2–3 weeks)
  - Define metric taxonomy + minimal set of required suites
  - Define threshold schema shape + versioning approach
  - Identify prompt set coverage gaps (especially tool-calling + structured output)
  - Decide enforcement location + failure/override policies

- Phase 1 (Build, ~4–6 weeks)
  - Control plane schema + CRUD storage for GuardrailPolicy
  - Eval runner service (async jobs, retries, timeouts, result persistence)
  - Eval-harness “gating mode” output format (structured)
  - Apply endpoint plumbing: observe-only logging first
  - Console UX: show gating status/results

- Phase 2 (Pilot, ~3–4 weeks)
  - Internal canary (top Optimize recommendations for Redwood-internal workloads)
  - Small set of design partners (choose quality-sensitive accounts)
  - Tune thresholds to reduce false positives/negatives
  - Validate safe-degrade behavior under induced failures

- Phase 3 (GA, ~2–4 weeks)
  - Default-on hard gating for targeted optimization types
  - Expand enforcement coverage
  - Post-launch retro + KPI readout

Risks / edge cases brainstorm (capture list; not all solved)
A) Timeouts and long-running evals
- Risk: eval runner latency/backlog blocks applies; customers perceive Optimize as “broken”.
- Specific edge cases:
  - Large prompt sets (or high token prompts) cause suite to exceed allowed runtime.
  - Multi-region routing changes require cross-region eval execution (adds latency).
  - Queue spikes during releases / model onboarding.
- Mitigations discussed:
  - Concurrency limits + separate eval capacity pool; isolate from customer traffic
  - Per-suite time budgets; partial results clearly labeled (but policy must treat as fail/blocked unless explicitly allowed)
  - Caching identical eval runs keyed by (model version, prompt-set rev, suite, config delta)

B) Flaky evals / nondeterminism
- Risk: a change is alternately pass/fail due to grader variance or non-deterministic ordering, leading to operator pain and eroding trust.
- Sources of flakiness:
  - Rubric graders / LLM-as-judge variance
  - Random seeds not pinned in harness
  - Non-deterministic metric ordering / serialization bugs
  - Prompt-set drift (prompts updated without revision pin)
- Mitigations:
  - Deterministic “gating mode” requirements (seed pinning where possible)
  - Min sample sizes; CI-aware thresholds
  - Sorting + schema validation in the policy evaluation layer
  - Strict version pinning: model version + prompt-set revision + harness version must be recorded and part of cache key

C) Model updates and compatibility
- Risk: same “model name” but different underlying build causes baseline drift.
- Edge cases:
  - Hosted model refresh changes behavior; gating compares to an outdated baseline.
  - Private deployments pin older runtime kernels; results differ.
  - Quantization profile not supported across all hardware / model variants.
- Mitigations:
  - Use immutable model version identifiers in gating inputs/outputs
  - Baseline strategy: compare candidate config vs current production config for that tenant/route/model version
  - Explicit “unsupported” classification distinct from “failed” (but still blocks apply)

D) Optimization-specific failure modes
- Quantization
  - Format drift: JSON keys missing/renamed; whitespace changes that break strict parsers
  - Reasoning degradation: lower task success on long-context prompts
  - Tool calls: malformed arguments, missing required fields
  - Known unsafe transitions (profile pairs) must be blocked regardless of eval results (policy-level denylist)
- Batching / continuous batching
  - Output ordering issues under streaming
  - Token-level latency changes causing client timeouts; customer interprets as “quality” issue
  - Tool-calling interleaving issues in multi-turn
- Caching
  - Prefix/KV cache collisions or incorrect reuse leading to “hallucinated” continuations
  - Cache effectiveness depends on prompt distribution; eval suite must represent realistic mix
- Routing tweaks
  - Model variant fallback changes semantics; eval suite must include “equivalence constraints” (how much change is acceptable?)

E) Customer-supplied prompt sets (PII + representativeness)
- Risk: customers can’t share real prompts; we end up gating on synthetic prompts that miss real regressions.
- Edge cases:
  - PII in prompt sets; storage and access control needed
  - Prompt sets too small to get reliable stats
  - Prompt sets overfit to easy cases (false confidence)
- Mitigations:
  - Provide redaction + allow customer-run in their environment (future); for now, clear guidance + minimal storage retention
  - Require minimum prompt count for certain metrics; otherwise show “insufficient sample size” and block or require override

F) UX / messaging / expectations
- Risk: “Apply blocked” becomes a support ticket magnet.
- UX questions:
  - How to explain “fail” vs “timeout” vs “system error” without overwhelming users?
  - What does the user do next? (rerun? edit prompt set? request override?)
  - How to show metric deltas + confidence in an understandable way?
- Agreement:
  - Always provide a next step
  - Provide a stable “Gating run summary” view with deep-link to artifacts

G) Observability + audit
- Risk: after-the-fact, we can’t prove gating ran or which thresholds were used.
- Requirements discussed:
  - Audit events for OptimizeConfigChange must include:
    - initiator (user/service)
    - config delta summary
    - gating decision + reasons
    - eval suite ids + versions, harness version
    - prompt-set revision ids
    - model version ids
    - override flags + justification + approver (if applicable)
  - Retention policy: keep enough fields for audit/compliance; avoid storing raw prompts in logs.

Open questions (owner / due date rough)
1) Baseline definition
- Q: what do we compare against: (A) current production config for that route, or (B) fixed “golden baseline” per model family?
- Leaning: A for correctness; B for global drift detection (nightly sentinel).
- Owner: Jonas / Selene.

2) Minimum initial metric set for V1
- Q: which metrics do we require for each optimization type to avoid scope creep?
- Proposed V1 minimum:
  - Structured output validity rate
  - Tool call schema adherence (where applicable)
  - Task success rubric for tagged workloads
  - Toxicity / policy guardrails (basic)
- Owner: Selene / Sana.

3) How strict should we be on timeouts?
- Q: treat timeout as fail (block) universally? Any tiers get “manual approval” state?
- Owner: Sean / Aditya.

4) Override approval model
- Q: do we require a second approver for overrides, or is “restricted role + justification + audit” sufficient?
- Owner: Naomi / Priya (needs leadership sign-off).

5) Prompt set coverage targets
- Q: how many prompts per workload tag do we need to be meaningful? What’s the minimum bar for pilot partners?
- Owner: Jonas.

Immediate action items
- Aditya: create Linear initiative + break out tickets for Phase 0 deliverables (already started: PM-842/843/844). Due: this week.
- Ethan/Jordan: draft ADR for enforcement point + failure modes (control plane gating) and circulate for comments. Due: 2024-11-25.
- Jonas/Selene/Sana: propose initial metric taxonomy + per-optimization required suites (one-pager) for V1. Due: 2024-11-27.
- Logan: quick pass on telemetry labels + cardinality risks for gating metrics; propose naming conventions. Due: 2024-11-27.
- Sean/Rafael: initial SRE rollout + alerting sketch (observe-only → soft-block → hard-block). Due: 2024-12-02.
- Kenji/Chloe: draft UI states and copy for pass/fail/timeout + links to artifacts. Due: 2024-12-02.

Notes to self / reminders
- Keep policy evaluation deterministic; “maybe” decisions will create repeated re-runs and undermine trust.
- Prioritize the failure modes we already see in support escalations (quantization + formatting/tool issues).
- Make the audit story excellent early (customers will ask for proof).
- Don’t let “perfect eval suite coverage” block shipping gating; ship minimal guardrails + iterate, but be conservative on enforcement when uncertain.
